additive: Red 40 / Allura Red AC / E129 / INS 129
india_status: Permitted in specified foods with maximum limit (FSSAI Regulations 2011)
eu_status: Permitted with mandatory warning label: 'May have an adverse effect on activity and attention in children' (EFSA Regulation EC 1333/2008)
note: EU requires mandatory Southampton warning for hyperactivity in children, while India and Australia permit under max limits without warning labels.
source: EFSA Scientific Opinion 2009; FSSAI Food Safety Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations; FSANZ Standard 1.3.1

india_status: Permitted as colouring agent under GMP / specified limits (FSSAI Regulations)
eu_status: Banned as food additive since 2022 (EU Regulation 2022/63 - genotoxicity concerns)
au_status: Currently permitted; reviewed by FSANZ (found safety concerns not substantiated for typical dietary intake)
note: Completely banned in EU due to particle accumulation and DNA damage concerns, but remains legal in India and Australia.
source: EFSA Panel on Food Additives and Flavourings (FAF) 2021; EU Commission Regulation 2022/63; FSANZ 2022 Statement

india_status: Banned in bread and bakery products since 2016 by FSSAI
eu_status: Banned across the EU (classified as potential carcinogen)
note: Prohibited across India, EU, and Australia due to carcinogenic classification by IARC.
source: FSSAI Notification June 2016; IARC Monographs Vol 73; FSANZ Food Standards Code

india_status: Permitted in specific food categories (max 100 mg/kg under FSSAI)
eu_status: Permitted but requires mandatory child hyperactivity warning label
au_status: Permitted under FSANZ Standard 1.3.1 with specific maximum levels
note: Synthetic azo dye requiring warning labels in EU for child attention impact; widely used in Indian sweets/packaged snacks.
source: EU Regulation 1333/2008 Annex V; FSSAI Standards Regulations 2011; FSANZ Standard 1.3.1

additive: Sunset Yellow FCF / Yellow 6 / E110 / INS 110
india_status: Permitted in specified foods with maximum limit (FSSAI)
eu_status: Permitted with mandatory child hyperactivity warning label; ADI reduced to 1 mg/kg bw
note: Part of the 'Southampton Six' colors requiring warning in Europe; permitted under standard limits in India and Australia.
source: EFSA Journal 2014;12(7):3765; FSSAI Chapter 3.2.1; FSANZ Schedule 15

india_status: Permitted as antioxidant in fats/oils up to 200 ppm (FSSAI)
eu_status: Permitted with strict limits (EFSA re-evaluated ADI 1.0 mg/kg bw)
au_status: Permitted under maximum levels in specified foods (FSANZ Standard 1.3.1)
note: Synthetic antioxidant allowed across regions within strict parts-per-million limits due to endocrine disruption investigations.
source: EFSA ANS Panel 2011; FSSAI Food Additives Regulations; FSANZ Code Schedule 15

india_status: Permitted in fats/oils and chewing gum (max 100-200 ppm)
eu_status: Permitted with reduced ADI (0.25 mg/kg bw)
note: Commonly paired with BHA; permitted with strict ADI caps across all three jurisdictions.
source: EFSA Journal 2012;10(3):2588; FSSAI Regulations 2011; FSANZ Schedule 15

india_status: Banned as a flour treatment agent / bleaching agent
eu_status: Banned for use in food and food-contact materials (Directive 2004/1/EC)
au_status: Banned for use as food additive in Australia/New Zealand
note: Prohibited in India, EU, and Australia due to thermal breakdown byproduct (semicarbazide).
source: FSSAI Gazette Notification; European Commission Directive 2004/1/EC; FSANZ

india_status: Permitted preservative Class II across multiple food categories (FSSAI)
eu_status: Permitted food additive with established ADI of 11 mg/kg bw (EFSA)
note: Widely permitted antimicrobial preservative across India, EU, and Australia with high safety consensus.
source: EFSA Journal 2019;17(3):5625; FSSAI Table 1 Preservatives; FSANZ Standard 1.3.1

india_status: Permitted Class II preservative in beverages/sauces up to specified limits (FSSAI)
eu_status: Permitted with strict max limits; caution advised when combined with Ascorbic Acid (Vitamin C)
au_status: Permitted under FSANZ Standard 1.3.1 with category limits
note: Permitted in all three jurisdictions; when combined with Vitamin C (ascorbic acid), can form trace benzene under heat/light.
source: EFSA ANS Panel 2016; FSSAI Regulations Schedule 1; FSANZ Standard 1.3.1

india_status: Permitted under GMP in specified foods; mandatory declaration 'Contains Added MSG' on label
eu_status: Permitted as flavour enhancer with group ADI of 30 mg/kg bw/day (EFSA)
au_status: Permitted flavour enhancer with mandatory ingredient declaration (FSANZ)
note: Permitted across all three jurisdictions under GMP/ADI; India specifically enforces mandatory front/back label declaration.
source: FSSAI Packaging & Labelling Reg 2.2.1; EFSA Journal 2017;15(7):4911; FSANZ Standard 1.2.4

india_status: Permitted non-nutritive sweetener; mandatory phenylketonurics advisory warning
eu_status: Permitted with ADI 40 mg/kg bw; mandatory warning for phenylketonuria sufferers
au_status: Permitted sweetener with mandatory warning statement for phenylalanine
note: Permitted across all 3 regions with universally mandatory 'Contains Phenylalanine / Not for Phenylketonurics' warning.
source: WHO/IARC/JECFA Evaluation 2023; EFSA 2013 Re-evaluation; FSSAI Rule 2.4.5; FSANZ Standard 1.2.3

india_status: Permitted artificial sweetener with category limits and mandatory label declaration
au_status: Permitted intense sweetener under FSANZ Standard 1.3.1
note: High-intensity sweetener permitted globally; requires 'Contains Non-Caloric Sweetener' declaration in India.
source: EFSA ANS Panel; FSSAI Food Safety Standards Regulations; FSANZ Standard 1.3.1

additive: Caramel Color Class IV (Ammonia Sulphite) / E150d / INS 150d
india_status: Permitted in carbonated beverages and foods under GMP / specified limits
eu_status: Permitted with group ADI 300 mg/kg bw; 4-MEI byproduct strictly monitored
au_status: Permitted coloring agent under FSANZ Standard 1.3.1
note: Permitted across all 3 regions with regulatory limits on trace byproduct 4-Methylimidazole (4-MEI).
source: EFSA Journal 2011;9(3):2004; FSSAI Food Additives Schedule; FSANZ Standard 1.3.1

india_status: Banned under FSSAI regulations for use in any food or beverage
au_status: Banned / Not permitted in Australia & New Zealand (FSANZ Standard 1.3.1)
note: Prohibited in India, EU, and Australia due to bromine bioaccumulation and organ toxicity concerns.
source: FSSAI Regulation 2.3.14; European Union Regulation EC 1333/2008; FSANZ Standard 1.3.1

india_status: Not approved for use in food products by FSSAI
eu_status: Not approved / Banned as a novel food ingredient in the EU
au_status: Not permitted under FSANZ Food Standards Code
note: Zero-calorie fat replacer prohibited in India, EU, and Australia due to gastrointestinal disruption and fat-soluble vitamin depletion.
source: FSSAI Non-Permitted Substances; EFSA Novel Foods Registry; FSANZ Standard 1.3.1
